A 18-year-old male presents to rapid care with ankle and knee discomfort following extensive walking
in flip-flops during weekend tourist activities. He denies any trauma but reports a persistent, dull ache.
The patient can fully bear weight, and physical examination shows no point tenderness. During an
osteopathic structural examination to assess for somatic dysfunction, you observe that the patient's
fibular head demonstrates increased anterolateral gliding compared to posteromedial movement during
certain foot motions. What is the most appropriate treatment setup and patient instruction for this
dysfunction? Answer Choices: (A) You would place their foot into plantarflexion and inversion to reach
the restrictive barrier, and then ask them to dorsiflex their foot against resistance (B) You would place
their foot into plantarflexion and eversion to reach the restrictive barrier, and then ask them to
plantarflex their foot against resistance (C) You would place their foot into dorsiflexion and inversion to
reach the restrictive barrier, and then ask them to evert their foot against resistance (D) You would
place their foot into dorsiflexion and eversion to reach the restrictive barrier, and ask them to plantarflex
their foot against resistance (E) You would position their leg to have the hip and knee flexed to 90
degrees, and with the foot dorsiflexed to the restrictive barrier you would ask them to plantarflex
against resistance (F) You would place their foot into plantarflexion and eversion to reach the restrictive
barrier, and then ask them to invert their foot against resistance (G) You would place their foot into
plantarflexion and eversion to reach the restrictive barrier, and then ask them to dorsiflex their foot
against resistance (H) You would place their foot into dorsiflexion and eversion to reach the restrictive
barrier, and then ask them to plantarflex their foot against resistance (I) You would place their foot into
dorsiflexion and inversion to reach the restrictive barrier, and then ask them to dorsiflex their foot
against resistance (J) You would place their foot into dorsiflexion and eversion to reach the restrictive
barrier, and then ask them to invert their foot against resistance
